title:
Space engineering
Space data links - Telecommand protocols, synchronization and channel coding
short_title: ECSS Telecommand Protocols, Sync and Coding (2008)
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Division
status_notes: Second issue (31 July 2008), following ECSS-E-50-04A (first issue, 14 November 2007); ECSS-E-50-04B was never issued (change log, p. 3). The document does not state that it is superseded. The library's later ECSS adoption notices state that it is replaced by ECSS-E-AS-50-24C (CCSDS 231.0-B-x), ECSS-E-AS-50-25C (CCSDS 232.0-B-x) and ECSS-E-AS-50-26C (CCSDS 232.1-B-x) (e.g. ECSS-E-AS-50-24C Rev.1, pp. 3 and 6).

key_points.text: Scope: data structures and protocols for a telecommand space data link and the physical layer operation procedure; normally ground-to-space, but usable for space-to-space links.

The stack comprises the segmentation sublayer, the transfer sublayer (with COP-1) and the synchronization and channel coding sublayer of the data link layer, plus the physical layer procedures at the sending end; security sublayers may be inserted by tailoring.
The TC Segment Header holds 2-bit Sequence Flags (bits 0-1) and a 6-bit MAP Identifier (bits 2-7), allowing up to 64 MAPs per virtual channel.
The optional Packet Assembly Controller pairs a data MAP (MAP ID MSB '0') with a control MAP (same ID with MSB '1'); on an exception it enters lockout until a MAP reset control segment is received.
A TC Transfer Frame consists of a 5-octet Primary Header, the Data Field and a 2-octet Frame Error Control Field, all always present; its length never exceeds 1024 octets and is at least 8 octets.

TC Primary Header fields: Transfer Frame Version Number 2 bits, Bypass Flag 1, Control Command Flag 1, Reserved Spare 2, Spacecraft Identifier 10, Virtual Channel Identifier 6, Frame Length 10 (bits 22-31), Frame Sequence Number 8.
The CLCW is 4 octets, conveyed in the Operational Control Field of a telemetry transfer frame; the No Bit Lock Flag is bit 17.
COP-1 control commands are carried in type-BC frames: Unlock is a single all-zeros octet; Set V(R) is three octets, '10000010', all zeros, then the new V(R) value.
A BCH codeblock is 8 octets: 56 information bits, 7 complemented parity bits from the (63,56) modified BCH code with g(x) = x^7 + x^6 + x^2 + 1, and a filler bit always '0'.
A CLTU is a 16-bit Start Sequence (EB90), Encoded Data (one or more BCH codeblocks carrying exactly one TC Transfer Frame) and an 8-octet Tail Sequence of seven C5 octets followed by 79.
The randomizer is used in all CLTUs, with h(x) = x^8 + x^6 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + x + 1 (period 255 bits); the bit transition generator stays all-ones until the Start Sequence is detected.
Codeblocks shall be decoded in error-correcting (SEC) mode: one bit in error is corrected and two are detected.
The acquisition sequence shall be at least 128 bits of alternating ones and zeros.
The idle sequence shall be at least 8 bits of alternating ones and zeros.
Carrier modulation modes: CMM-1 unmodulated carrier, CMM-2 acquisition sequence, CMM-3 telecommand data (CLTU), CMM-4 idle sequence.
PLOP-2 should be used in preference to PLOP-1 because it supports a higher data throughput; with PLOP-2 a minimum idle sequence of one octet is inserted between CLTUs.

Changes from ESA-PSS-04-107: blocking of packets, VCs without segments, no authentication or Segment Trailer, maximum frame length 1024 instead of 256 octets, COP-1B instead of COP-1A, a different Tail Sequence, randomization added, only 64-bit codeblocks and PLOP-1 added.

Differences from CCSDS: the PAC (so segments can be one octet), exactly one frame per CLTU, mandatory FECF (minimum frame 8 instead of 6 octets), always accepting a one-bit error in the Start Sequence, mandatory randomization and SEC, mandatory idle between CLTUs in PLOP-2 and a defined No Bit Lock Flag.
Annex D gives frame rejection and undetected error performance for channel bit error rates of 10^-4, 10^-5 and 10^-6, assuming PLOP-2 on an AWGN binary symmetric channel.

notes: Unlike its sister standards, the foreword does not name a working group. Superseded by ECSS-E-AS-50-24C, -25C and -26C (all in the library; the CCSDS books they adopt, ccsds-231-0-231x0b4e1, ccsds-232-0-232x0b4e1c1 and ccsds-232-1-232x1b2e2c1, are also in the library). The normative CCSDS 135.0-B-3 is in the library at the later issue CCSDS 135.0-B-4 (ccsds-135-0-135x0b4s), and the FSP book at CCSDS 912.3-B-3 (ccsds-912-3-912x3b3s). Predecessor ESA-PSS-04-107 Issue 2 (April 1992) is in the library as esa-pss-04-107-issue2-april1992. The extraction uses Unicode non-breaking hyphens (U+2011) in document IDs. Figures (frame and CLCW formats, encoder, state diagrams, CMM sequences) are images; the CMM table is on p. 125. Clause 3.3 cites 'ECSS-ST-00-01' (p. 15) for ECSS-S-ST-00-01, and its NOTE names 'AC, CB and BD frames' where AD, BC and BD are meant. The bibliography gives CCSDS 320.0-B-4 as 'Issue 3, January 2006' (p. 155). Annex B prints 'PLOP_2' (p. 133). Superscripts are flattened in the text ('x7 + x6'). Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers; srcgrep shows 156 PDF pages (the last one blank) while the registry gives 155.
